solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Southwark infirmary for men only?

parts.note: a famous London teaching hospital in Southwark whose name, read literally, suggests a hospital for chaps alone

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether a south London hospital admits only male patients.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital is named after its founder, Thomas Guy; the question mark invites reading 'guys' as 'men'. Southwark is a borough of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known teaching hospital in Southwark, London, founded by Thomas Guy, carries this name.

clue.text: Open University head under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for head is placed below the letters for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
the head of something is its front

explanation.surface: A news item about who leads the Open University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' reads as the institution, but 'Open' is the definition and 'University' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and frank is being open, a sense the answer shares as an adjective.

clue.text: Gain an advantage over nervous marshal at once

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and agitated, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A jittery military marshal is overtaken by an opponent all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' rearranges the letters of MARSHAL AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means getting ahead of a rival by acting first, i.e. to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Fruit: love assortment

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
a range of goods is an assortment of them

explanation.surface: A fruit seller's sign promising a lovely mixed selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit, the common example of the category named.

clue.text: Game in which castle, perhaps, should be moved

indicators.note: letters that should be moved are shifted into new positions, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to describe chess, where a castle (rook) is a piece to be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' suggests the chess piece, but 'castle, perhaps' is simply anagram fodder for 'should be moved'. The game is a British children's party game where a wrapped package goes round the circle while music plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British children's party game of handing a wrapped package round until the music stops.

clue.text: Find and copy

definitions.meaning: to find or track down something lost
to copy a drawing by following its lines through thin paper

explanation.surface: Two verbs joined, like an instruction in a search task.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to track down and to reproduce an outline through overlaid paper.

clue.text: Tolerant of knight that is breaking fast

indicators.note: the knight and that-is letters break into the word for fast, splitting it apart

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
N is the chess notation for a knight
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A knight is forgiving towards someone who breaks a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is the Christian season of abstinence before Easter, not speed; 'breaking' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is permissive and forgiving of others' faults is lenient; 'of' is a link word.

clue.text: Bed starts to creak — replace its base

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words, creak, replace, its, base, are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A creaky bed whose base needs replacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' looks like a verb phrase (begins to creak), but it takes the first letter of each of the following four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's cot, a small bed with barred sides, is also called by this word.

clue.text: Anger about female bringing weapon

indicators.note: the word for anger goes about, i.e. around, the letter for female

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Fury at a woman who has brought a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun fired from the shoulder, a type of firearm.

clue.text: Do without it, as ban involved

indicators.note: involved means intricate and tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Giving something up because a prohibition is in force.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or hold back from something, especially an indulgence, is to go without it.

clue.text: Sold illicitly from sack by stage

parts.note: to boot someone out is to sack them
a leg of a journey or race is a stage of it

explanation.surface: Goods sold under the counter, straight out of a sack beside a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband goods, especially liquor or recordings, made and traded illegally are described this way.

clue.text: Subject of article — me!

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed writer insisting the article is all about them.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a talk or piece of writing is its subject.

clue.text: Working spell without delay

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A work stint that runs to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving punctually means arriving with no lateness, so the phrase means promptly.

clue.text: Partly coincide as regards circuit

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A query about whether two races share part of their route.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that extend over part of the same space or time share a portion in common.

clue.text: Dictator in regiment's HQ receiving head of state

indicators.note: the word for the headquarters receives, i.e. takes in, the extra letter

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters or base

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tyrant at military headquarters entertaining a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts S, from 'head of state', inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with absolute power, often cruel, is a tyrant or autocrat.

clue.text: Take undue advantage of don covering at university

indicators.note: the phrase for don covers, i.e. goes around, the word for at university

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
being up at Oxford or Cambridge means being at university

explanation.surface: A university lecturer exploited while covering for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a university teacher but is the verb meaning to dress in; 'covering' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone's good nature, imposing on them unfairly, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Peninsula in Russian region son overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means missed out, so the letter for son is dropped

parts.note: Siberia is the vast region of northern Asian Russia

explanation.surface: A peninsula somewhere in Russia that a son failed to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal sit on the large south-west European landmass with sea on three sides.

clue.text: Wife leaving joiner for church officer

indicators.note: the letter for wife leaves, so it is removed from the word for joiner

parts.note: a welder joins pieces of metal together

explanation.surface: A woman abandons her carpenter husband for a church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is someone who joins metal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian and other churches, a lay official who helps govern the congregation holds this title.

clue.text: Wee drink ahead of a play

indicators.note: the word for the drink comes ahead of, before, the letter a

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, especially whisky

explanation.surface: A quick whisky before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A play performed on stage is a work of the theatre, a piece for acting.

clue.text: Lucky dip bishop organised, backing nevertheless also required

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run an event is to organise it

indicators.note: backing means the word for nevertheless is read backwards

parts.note: but can mean nevertheless or however

explanation.surface: A bishop runs the lucky dip at a church fete, though he needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: A lucky dip is a fairground game where prizes are hidden in a container of bran or sawdust and fished out at random.
explanation.definitionFit: The tub of bran with hidden prizes at a British fete is itself the lucky-dip game.

clue.text: I must go in club that offers inducement

indicators.note: the letter I must go in, i.e. be inserted into, the word for club

parts.note: a bat, as used in cricket, is a kind of club

explanation.surface: A sports club offering incentives to new members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society but is a striking implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offered to lure or tempt, like food on a hook, is a lure or enticement.

clue.text: One who wrote nonsense about the kid, perhaps

indicators.note: the poet's name goes about, around, the word the

parts.note: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A nonsense poet writing about a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' suggests a child, but it is the soft skin of a young goat; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is fine soft material made from young goatskin, one example of tanned hide.

clue.text: Better run island, one in the Bay of Naples

definitions.text: one in the Bay of Naples

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Advice to manage an island more effectively, with a nod to the Bay of Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better run' reads as an adjective and verb, but 'Better' is the verb to outdo. 'island' looks like the definition but gives only I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky Italian isle off the Sorrento coast, famed for the Blue Grotto, lies in that bay.

clue.text: Staightforward procedures involving one in poor health

indicators.note: the word for procedures involves, i.e. takes in, the letter for one

parts.note: plans are schemes or procedures for doing something
I is the Roman numeral one
ailing means unwell, in poor health

explanation.surface: Simple routines followed by someone unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts I inside PLANS. 'Staightforward' is the clue's typo for straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means easy progress with no difficulties, so it describes something simple.
